comments:
actually, it returns an `AnsibleFilterError` after capturing/bypassing  the `TypeError`

The fix would be to actually emit the TypeError from filters as we do handle it for the Undefined case in there already.

review_comments: Overall, I think this change fixes the problem well. I'm just not sure about the pros/cons of having a custom exception inherit from multiple exceptions, one custom and one built it. It may be ok, I'm just not sure.

```
BaseException
  +-- Exception
  |     +-- TypeError
  |           +-- AnsibleFilterTypeError
  +-- AnsibleError
        +-- AnsibleRuntimeError
              +-- AnsibleTemplateError
                    +-- AnsibleFilterTypeError
```
its only way to thread needle between us capturing typeerror and reusing on the 'undefined case' and still passing through as a filter error whichalso has it's own special handling.
